# Drift Patterns

A taxonomy of every drift type that can occur between code tokens and Figma variable bindings, with detection signals and fix recipes.

---

## 1. Value drift 🔴

**What it is:** The same semantic concept is named the same on both sides, but the resolved values differ.

**Detection:** Resolve Figma variable chain to final value → compare to the value generated by Style Dictionary for the same CSS var.

**Examples seen:**
- `theme/typography/label/font-weight` resolved to `500` in Figma vs `600` in code. Root cause: a `font-weight/500` Foundation variable was added to Figma and the semantic alias was updated to point to it instead of `font-weight/600`.

**Fix (Code → Figma):**
Find the Foundation variable that holds the wrong value and update the semantic alias to point to the correct one:

```javascript
const correctFoundationVar = allVars.find(v => v.name === 'typography/font-weight/600');
const semanticVar = allVars.find(v => v.name === 'theme/typography/label/font-weight');
for (const mode of semanticCollection.modes) {
  semanticVar.setValueForMode(mode.modeId, figma.variables.createVariableAlias(correctFoundationVar));
}
```

**Fix (Figma → Code):** Identify the resolved value, find the Foundation token that holds it, update the semantic token reference in `semantic.tokens.json`.

---

## 2. Naming drift 🟠

**What it is:** The same concept is bound on both sides but the token names follow a different structure. Values may match but paths don't.

**Examples seen:**
- Code used `--ds-theme-typography-font-family-body` (property→role), Figma used `theme/typography/label/font-family` (role→property). After restructuring to role-first DTCG, both sides aligned.
- Code used `--ds-theme-typography-heading-fontFamily` (camelCase), Figma used `theme/typography/heading/font-family` (kebab path).

**Detection:** After applying the naming bridge, the code var converts to a Figma path that doesn't exist — but a variable with the same resolved value does exist under a different path.

**Fix:** Depends on which side is source of truth:
- **Code is source:** Update the Figma component's binding to the variable that matches the code's naming convention.
- **Figma is source:** Update the CSS var reference in the component CSS module to the new name, and ensure the semantic token exists in `semantic.tokens.json`.

---

## 3. Missing binding in Figma 🟡

**What it is:** Code sets a CSS property with a token, but the corresponding Figma node has no variable bound to that property.

**Examples seen:**
- `border-width` was not bound in Figma until `border-width/1` was created and bound to `strokeWeight`.
- `letter-spacing` was not set in code until the `typography.letter-spacing.0` token was added.

**Detection:** Code has `var(--ds-X)`, but scanning Figma bindings finds no binding for the corresponding visual property on any node.

**Fix (Code → Figma):**
Find the node (typically the main frame/input element) and bind the variable:

```javascript
// For stroke weight
const bwVar = allVars.find(v => v.name === 'border-width/1');
inputNode.setBoundVariable('strokeWeight', figma.variables.createVariableAlias(bwVar));

// For fill (background)
const bgVar = allVars.find(v => v.name === 'theme/color/background/default');
inputNode.setBoundVariable('fills', figma.variables.createVariableAlias(bgVar));
```

**Caution:** Not every CSS property has a direct Figma equivalent. `outline`, `opacity`, `transition`, `cursor` — these have no Figma variable binding. Flag but do not attempt to bind.

---

## 4. Missing token in code 🟡

**What it is:** Figma has a variable bound on a node, but code doesn't set the corresponding CSS property at all (relying on inheritance or Mantine defaults).

**Examples seen:**
- Figma bound `theme/typography/label/line-height` on the label text node; code's `.label` class didn't set `line-height`.
- Figma bound `theme/typography/small/font-weight` on description text; code's `.description` didn't set `font-weight`.

**Detection:** Figma binding exists, but scanning the component CSS finds no `var(--ds-...)` for the corresponding property on that element's class.

**Fix (Figma → Code):** Add the CSS property to the relevant class in the component's `.module.css`:
```css
.label {
  line-height: var(--ds-theme-typography-label-line-height);
}
```

**Fix (Code → Figma):** If intentionally relying on inheritance (e.g. font-family set on root), decide whether to remove the Figma binding or add an explicit code declaration.

---

## 5. Raw Foundation token in Figma 🔴

**What it is:** A Figma component binding points directly to a Foundation (tier-1) variable instead of going through a Semantic (tier-2) alias.

**Examples seen:**
- `itemSpacing` on TextInput bound to `spacing/4` (Foundation) instead of `theme/spacing/gap-xs` (Semantic).
- `paddingTop` bound to `spacing/8` (Foundation) instead of a semantic spacing token.

**Detection:** Figma binding variable name has no `theme/` prefix.

**Fix (Code → Figma):** Create the missing semantic token first (in `semantic.tokens.json`), rebuild tokens, then update the Figma binding to the new semantic variable:

```javascript
const semanticVar = allVars.find(v => v.name === 'theme/spacing/gap-xs');
for (const variant of set.children) {
  variant.setBoundVariable('itemSpacing', figma.variables.createVariableAlias(semanticVar));
}
```

**When to accept raw Foundation tokens in Figma:** Heading font sizes (h1–h6) are intentionally tier-1 references in `title.module.css` because no single semantic "heading role" covers all 6 levels. This is documented and acceptable.

---

## 6. Structural / organisation drift 🟠

**What it is:** The token hierarchy on one side doesn't match the other — usually caught during a larger refactor.

**Examples seen:**
- Code changed from flat `font-family.body` / `font-size.label` structure to role-first `label.font-family` / `label.font-size`. Figma already used role-first.
- The h1–h6 composite tokens (`$type: "typography"`) existed in code but were filtered from CSS output — the CSS module was referencing vars that were never emitted.

**Detection:** CSS vars in the component reference token paths that don't appear in the generated `tokens.css`. Or Figma uses a different grouping depth than code.

**Fix:** Requires coordinated update of `semantic.tokens.json`, the component CSS files, and Figma bindings. Use the full restructure approach (as done in the typography refactor session).

---

## 7. Variant coverage gap 🟡

**What it is:** Code implements a variant that has no corresponding Figma component variant, or vice versa.

**Examples seen:**
- Button has `filled` and `outline` variants in code, but Figma only had `State=Default/Hover/Disabled` (no `outline` variant at all).

**Detection:** Compare code's variant prop values against Figma component set children names.

**Fix (Code → Figma):** Generate the missing Figma variant using the figma-component-generator skill.
**Fix (Figma → Code):** Add the variant to the TSX props and CSS module.

---

## 8. Un-tokenized Mantine base style vs. Figma "no property" 🔴

**What it is:** Mantine's own compiled CSS (`@mantine/core/styles/*.css`) sets a visual
property (fill, border, etc.) using Mantine's own theme variables (`--mantine-color-*`),
not a `--ds-*` token. Neither side's extraction catches it: code-side scanning only looks
for `var(--ds-*)` in our `.module.css` / `vars` prop, and Figma correctly has no binding
(or `fills: []`) for that property — so there's nothing to compare on either side, and
the audit reports "in sync" by omission.

**Examples seen:**
- Checkbox's `.input` had no `background-color` override. Mantine's `Checkbox.css` sets
  `:where([data-mantine-color-scheme='light']) .m_26063560 { background-color:
  var(--mantine-color-white); }` on the unchecked input — giving it an opaque white fill.
  Figma's `Unchecked, State=Default` Control has `fills: []` (no fill, transparent) and
  `checkbox.layla` confirms only `.stroke(...)`, no `.color(...)`. Radio has the identical
  pattern via `Radio.css`'s `.m_8a3dbb89` base rule.

**Detection:** For each component, grep the relevant `@mantine/core/styles/*.css` file
for base (non-`:checked`/`:disabled`) rules on the styles-API class that sets
`background-color`/`border-color`/`color` from a `--mantine-*` variable, and check
whether our `.module.css` overrides it. Cross-reference against the Figma binding (or
absence of one) for the equivalent property on the corresponding node.

**Fix (Figma → Code or Layla → Code):** Add an explicit override in the component's
`.module.css` — e.g. `background-color: transparent;` to neutralize Mantine's default,
or `background-color: var(--ds-theme-color-...)` if Figma/Layla specify an actual fill.
Verify specificity: Mantine's `:checked`/`:disabled` rules are typically `(0,2,0)` and
will still win over a base-class `(0,1,0)` override, so this is safe to add without
breaking other states — but confirm with a rendered screenshot.

---

## Property-to-Figma-binding map

Reference for which CSS properties correspond to which Figma `boundVariables` keys:

| CSS property | Figma `boundVariables` key |
|---|---|
| `background-color` / `fill` | `fills` |
| `border-color` / `stroke` | `strokes` |
| `border-width` / stroke weight | `strokeWeight` or `strokeTopWeight` etc. |
| `border-radius` (all corners) | `topLeftRadius`, `topRightRadius`, `bottomLeftRadius`, `bottomRightRadius` |
| `color` (text) | `fills` on TEXT node |
| `font-size` | `fontSize` on TEXT node |
| `font-family` | `fontFamily` on TEXT node |
| `font-weight` | `fontWeight` on TEXT node |
| `line-height` | `lineHeight` on TEXT node |
| `letter-spacing` | `letterSpacing` on TEXT node |
| `padding-left/right` | `paddingLeft`, `paddingRight` |
| `padding-top/bottom` | `paddingTop`, `paddingBottom` |
| `gap` / `column-gap` / `row-gap` | `itemSpacing` |
| `width` | `width` (when fixed) |
| `height` | `height` (when fixed) |
| `opacity` | no variable binding in Figma |
| `box-shadow` | no variable binding (shadows are not variables in Figma) |
